not_testable.statement: S100.2 adds THREE FIELDS TO EVERY PLAY - `requires`, `scope`, `forward_evidence`. RATIONALE, load-bearing: most blind-versus-refined disagreements are not disagreements about the market at all, they are differences in what was KNOWABLE at decision time, and treating them as a precedence problem hides that. `requires` (open_time_only / needs_day_N-1_tape / needs_intraday_reveal) names the information a play consumes and dissolves those apparent conflicts. `scope` (leg side / day net / block lean / magnitude / gap / timing) names what a play OWNS, which is the correct precedence axis and the one S97.2 already settled when it gave R2 the post-print leg side and magnitude while the chain kept the day net. `forward_evidence` records whether a play has been confirmed on a block it was NOT derived from, and it is the field that GATES PROMOTION: refined rules are hindsight-fitted and carry zero forward evidence, so they must NEVER silently overwrite blind-applicable ones. Doing so would promote in-sample fits into the operating playbook untested, and it would destroy the blind-versus-refined GAP, which is itself the measurement of how much of the edge is sequential rather than open-time (G7 was 3/10 blind against 9/10 refined; R2 was 4/10 blind against 10/10 refined; G11 is 6/12 blind against 10/12 refined). A refined rule earns open-time status only by surviving a forward block. WHERE TWO PLAYS OVERLAP IN SCOPE WITHOUT A SETTLED BOUNDARY, THE OVERLAP IS FLAGGED RATHER THAN RESOLVED - see s100_2_scope_overlaps_flagged.
